subject: Hosted API — bulk rate proposal and SLA tradeoffs
messages:
From: Ari Patel <ari@brightcart.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-27T14:32:00-05:00
Subject: Hosted API pricing for 500M+ tokens / latency SLOs

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the quick demo earlier — BrightCart is excited about Redwood's prefix caching and the consistency you showed for catalog generation. We're trying to build a baseline costing model and need to understand hosted pricing for sustained, high-volume usage. Ballpark: 400-700M tokens/month with short bursts up to ~1.5B tokens in holiday windows.

Key asks:
- Baseline per-1k-token cost for hosted API (standard generation path) and how that steps down with volume.
- Any committed-volume discounts vs. pay-as-you-go.
- SLA/latency guarantees you can reasonably offer for 95th percentile under sustained load (we target ~200ms p95 for short deltas).
- Options for burst credits or pre-purchased token buckets for seasonal spikes.

We'd like a short written proposal we can share with procurement — a single-page summary and a simple table of tiered unit prices would be ideal. Can you send something by early next week?

Thanks,
Ari Patel
Head of ML Products
BrightCart

---
Attachment: (none)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Ari Patel <ari@brightcart.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing for 500M+ tokens / latency SLOs

Hi Ari — great to hear, and thanks for the clarity on volume shape. I'm attaching a concise proposal and a short SLA/credits spreadsheet that sketches a few commitment levels (monthly committed tokens) and burst credit mechanics.

High-level summary in this email:
- Pay-as-you-go baseline: $0.0035 per 1K tokens (generation path) — suggested as retail baseline.
- Volume tiers (committed monthly):
  * 0-50M: baseline
  * 50M-250M: 15% discount off baseline
  * 250M-600M: 30% discount off baseline
  * 600M+: 42% discount off baseline (requires 3- or 12-month commit)
- Burst credits: pre-purchased token credits that convert at the committed tier rate and can be consumed in any month; unused credits roll forward for up to 3 months.
- SLA: Hosted API SLA for p95 latency at committed throughput: 99.5% monthly availability; financial credits available for outages >SLA. For strict 200ms p95 across sustained 1.5B bursts we recommend a Dedicated capacity conversation — hosted can get close with higher committed tiers + routing policy.

I'll loop in Lauren for the precise discount language and to confirm what flex we can offer on the 600M+ band. If this looks directionally right, I'll send a cleaned PDF that procurement can review.

Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_hosted_bulk_proposal_v1.pdf, SLA_credits_table.xlsx
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-29T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Internal — BrightCart pricing ask (HS-1298)

Ben / Lauren,

Ari at BrightCart wants a short procurement-ready proposal for ~400-700M mo sustained, with holiday bursts to ~1.5B. My suggested bands above are in the draft I shared. We need to confirm:

1) Is the 42% at 600M+ reasonable as an upper shelf for hosted? They prefer hosted for now but will tolerate Dedicated if the economics justify the lift.
2) Can we offer a 6-month commit (vs. 12) for the 600M+ band with slightly lower discount (say 38%)?
3) Any guardrails on p95 latency credits wording we should not overpromise in a hosted contract?

Pricing considerations I think we should bake into the short doc: token-based unit, committed vs. PAYG mapping, burst credit conversion, and explicit performance caveat pointing them to Dedicated for <200ms p95 at sustained holiday scale.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call.

Jonas
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-30T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal — BrightCart pricing ask (HS-1298)

Jonas — quick thoughts from pricing:

- 42% off baseline at 600M+ is borderline but defensible if we require a 12-month commit or prepayment. For 6-months, back it down to 36-38% and require a minimum monthly ACH/credit commit.
- For PAYG, $0.0035/1K is fine as list. If they sign a 3- or 6-month commit we should include an early-termination recoup clause tied to consumed tokens vs. committed tokens.
- Burst credits: allow them to buy "burst buckets" at the committed tier rate (no further discounts) and permit 3 months of carryover. This keeps accounting simple.
- SLA language: keep hosted SLA focused on availability and request-level success; avoid hard latency guarantees in the hosted contract — offer a performance SLO advisory and a migration path to Dedicated for 200ms p95 promises. You can offer a non-financial performance credit (e.g., extended support hours) instead of dollar credits for latency misses.

If procurement pushes back we can offer a one-time onboarding credit (up to $25k) or a small intro discount on the first two months.

-ben
Head of Pricing Ops
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Ari Patel <ari@brightcart.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-31T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API pricing for 500M+ tokens / latency SLOs

Hi Ari — thanks again. Per our thread and internal alignment, attached is a short proposal PDF and an XLS with the SLA/credits sketch. Highlights:

- PAYG baseline: $0.0035 / 1K tokens.
- Committed discounts: 15% (50-250M), 30% (250-600M), 36% (600M+ for 6-month commit) / 42% (600M+ for 12-month prepay).
- Burst credits: pre-purchase at committed tier; carry-forward up to 3 months.
- SLA: Hosted SLA covers availability and error-rate credits. We do not offer strict latency financial credits on hosted at scale — we can provide a performance advisory and migration path to Dedicated if 200ms p95 is a hard requirement.
- Flex: Intro onboarding credit of up to $20k for HS-1298 if you sign a 6-month commit by 2026-02-15.

Proposed next step: 30-minute procurement + legal sync Tuesday 2/2 to walk the one-pager and attachables. Does 10am PT work for you?

Thanks — attaching the docs now.

Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0148
